Data #cat-data

<BarChart/>

Vertical bars, one per datum. The value floats above each bar's own growing top.

kit/DataCharts.jsx

The value label is an absolutely positioned span pinned to the SAME percentage that sizes the fill beneath it — `bottom: {pct}%` on the label, `height: {pct}%` on the fill, one shared variable. That is what lets it track the bar's current top through the grow transition instead of sitting fixed at the height of the tallest possible bar.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
data array<{label,value,color?}> [{"label":"Submitted","value":24}, {"label":"Triage","value":18}, … {"label":"Closed","value":3}] one bar per item — value sets the fill height as a % of the tallest bar in the set
color string "var(--chart-3)" literal CSS colour on every bar, no cycling; a per-datum `d.color` still wins over it
height number 160 pixel height of the plotting area, written straight into `style`
format (value) => node (v) => `${v} claims` formats the value label floating above each bar

markup 
<p class="m-0 py-6 text-center text-sm text-muted-foreground">No data.</p>

Plain `gap-2`, not `gap-bar` — the data-bar anatomy utilities (`h-bar`, `gap-bar`, `min-w-label`/`max-w-label`, `min-w-value`) are for the horizontal ROW primitives (HBars, FunnelChart, StackedBar); a vertical bar has no label column and no fixed row height to size, so none of them apply here.

<HBars/>

Ranked horizontal bars — ModelChart's own row, generalised to pre-aggregated data.

kit/DataCharts.jsx

The row is label · track · rounded fill · mono value, because that row is already the token-native answer to "one labelled bar" and there is no reason to invent a second one. `sort={false}` keeps the caller's order instead of ranking by value — right for a pipeline or a priority ladder, where re-ordering by count would scramble a sequence that is supposed to read top to bottom in a fixed way.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
data array<{label,value,color?}> [{"label":"Submitted","value":24}, {"label":"Triage","value":18}, … {"label":"Closed","value":3}] one row per item
sort boolean false true (default) ranks by value; false keeps the caller's order
max number 8 row cap — the array is sliced, not scrolled
color string "var(--chart-6)" literal override, every row
format (value) => node (v) => `${v} claims` formats the mono value at the row's end

The groove is `bg-track`, not `bg-muted` — a dedicated token even though the two happen to share a value under Beacon today (whose own doc defines muted as "donut and bar tracks" too); keeping them separate is what lets the groove move independently if a future page gives it its own value. 2026-08-13 — the row at the series max takes `--gradient-data`; every other row is flat `--chart-6`, not its own step of the ramp. Both specimens below use the SAME CLAIM_STAGES data as BarChart, and since that fixture is already in descending order, `sort` and `sort={false}` render identically here — the prop still does something, this fixture just can't show it.

<LineChart/>

Line or area trend, one series or two, with dots that live outside the SVG on purpose.

kit/DataCharts.jsx

`preserveAspectRatio="none"` deliberately stretches the 0–100 square viewBox to fill a wide, short card — that non-uniform stretch is what lets the line reach every point correctly, and a straight line survives it fine (an affine transform keeps a line straight). A round marker does not: an SVG `<circle>` at this box's typical aspect comes out several times wider than tall, because `vector-effect="non-scaling-stroke"` only protects a shape's stroke WIDTH from the scale, never its geometry.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
data array<{label,value}> [{"label":"Mon","value":4}, {"label":"Tue","value":7}, … {"label":"Sun","value":1}] needs ≥2 points; each becomes one SVG coordinate, one HTML dot and one tooltip column
compare array<{label,value}> [{"label":"Mon","value":6}, {"label":"Tue","value":5}, … {"label":"Sun","value":3}] the prior period, drawn BEHIND the current series at 80% on --color-border — "context, not a peer." Sliced to data's length; scaled on the SAME extent as `data` — two lines on independent axes is a chart that lies
area boolean true a real vertical gradient fill under the line — the stroke colour at 24% opacity fading to 0% at the baseline
dots boolean true point markers — real HTML circles (8px, 2px border), not SVG, for the reason above. Dim to .35 opacity for every point but the hovered one when tooltip is pinned; undimmed otherwise
grid boolean true three dashed rules at 25/50/75% reading `stroke-gray-2` — a divider on white, quiet enough to sit behind the line without competing with it
tooltip boolean true in a prototype: keep the pinned markup and move it from your script; the invisible column buttons are the hit targets
seriesLabel / compareLabel string "This period" / "Last period" the tooltip's two row names
color / compareColor string "var(--chart-1)" / "var(--color-border)" flat overrides; neither cycles, neither takes a -grad fallback
format (v) => node (v) => `${v} claims` formats each series' figure in the tooltip
height number 190 pixel height of the whole chart, day labels included

So the dots are real HTML circles, positioned OUTSIDE the distorted SVG coordinate space with plain CSS percentages instead — the same [x,y] numbers the path uses, reused as [left%,top%] with no conversion, because the box is 100 units square in intent. This is an inherited defect from Charts.jsx corrected here, never caught in the original because Charts.jsx had zero callers and was never actually rendered. Neither series ever cycles and neither falls back to a `-grad` token — the area fill's own vertical gradient (the stroke colour at 24% opacity fading to 0% at the baseline) already gives the wash a gradient reads for, without borrowing a token documented for bar fills. THE TOOLTIP IS THE ONE PLACE THIS CATALOG AND THE BUILT APP LEGITIMATELY DIFFER: the component shows it on hover or focus of an invisible per-point column; a snippet has no hover state, so the specimen below pins it at Thursday. Same markup, same classes, same tokens — copy it, then drive `left`/`top` and the two figures from whichever point your script decides is active. It is positioned in the undistorted overlay space for exactly the reason the dots are. 2026-08-13 — five corrections found against DataCharts.jsx: the grid's three dashed rules read `stroke-gray-2` (this doc always said so; the snippet's own class had drifted to `stroke-border`), the compare series is `--color-border` at 80% opacity — not `--chart-2` at 55%, which is `--color-secondary` and reads as a near-black peer rather than quiet context — drawn behind the current series so it can never cover it; the area fill is a real two-stop `<linearGradient>` (24%→0% opacity), not a flat 12%-opacity wash; point markers are 8px (`h-2 w-2`) with a 2px (`border-2`) border, not 7px/1.5px, and every point but the active one dims to .35 opacity when the tooltip is pinned (undimmed, at 1, when it isn't); and the tooltip's own text read `text-background` — `--color-canvas`, the page ground, not `--color-surface`'s white — invisible-by-coincidence on the dark `bg-secondary` card underneath it.

<GaugeRing/>

Radial gauge for a single ratio.

kit/DataCharts.jsx

Two concentric circles, both fixed radius 54 on a 140×140 viewBox: a plain groove reading `stroke-track`, and a progress circle whose `stroke-dasharray`/`stroke-dashoffset` pair draws the ratio, rotated -90° so the arc starts at 12 o'clock instead of 3.

value number 11 the numerator
max number 16 the denominator; the ratio is clamped to [0,1]

sublabel string "of 16" second line inside the ring, under the percentage
color string "var(--chart-1)" ring stroke only. Ignored when tone is set
tone "success" · "warning" · "info" · "danger" "success" OPTIONAL. Tints groove (-bg), ring (-dot, falling back to -ink) and figure (-ink) together
size number 150 pixel width of the outer wrapper

The groove token is the same one HBars' track reads — `stroke-track` resolves through the identical `--color-track` role as `bg-track`, so a gauge's empty arc and a bar's empty groove always agree under all three languages. Single-series like LineChart: `color` is a flat override, never a ramp cycle. 2026-08-13 — `tone` added: it tints groove (-bg), ring (-dot, falling back to -ink) and figure (-ink) together, the same three-part split Card/StatTile's own tone prop uses. Opt-in and additive — no tone renders exactly as it always has, so "the groove always reads stroke-track" above is now the untoned case specifically, not an unconditional rule.

<FunnelChart/>

Descending stages, tapering by value, caller order preserved.

kit/DataCharts.jsx

One deliberate deviation from Charts.jsx: the original printed the value INSIDE the coloured bar. That only stays legible if every fill in the ramp has a known, safe contrast against one ink — true of a single hand-picked palette, false of independent theme ramps (an amber step cannot always hold white, and nothing here can promise chart-5 in a language not yet written is any different). The value sits OFF the fill instead, the same precedent ModelChart already set, so no per-render contrast problem is ever re-opened.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
data array<{label,value,color?}> [{"label":"Submitted","value":24}, {"label":"Triage","value":18}, … {"label":"Closed","value":3}] caller order preserved — a funnel is a sequence, never re-ranked
color string "var(--chart-2)" literal override, every stage
format (value) => node (v) => `${v} claims` formats the mono value beside each bar — never inside it

The row is a flex line, not a grid — it used to be `grid-cols-[minmax(0,6rem)_1fr_2.5rem]`, which capped the label track at 6rem, BELOW `max-w-label`'s 7rem, so both label utilities were inert and the value column was a hard-coded 2.5rem instead of the token's minimum. The label and value are minimums that grow, and "the track absorbs the difference" is a flex-line rule by definition. Bars are centred (`margin-inline: auto`) and clamped to a 10% floor so a stage near zero still reads as a bar, not a sliver.

<Heatmap/>

Intensity grid — four discrete warm buckets by value, not a continuous mix.

kit/DataCharts.jsx

FOUR discrete buckets, not the old continuous `color-mix()` gradient — DataCharts.dc.html: "a per-cell color-mix against the ramp produces dozens of near-identical oranges no legend can explain; four buckets can be read off the key." Each cell quantises into thirds of its value's share of the series max — bucket 0 reserved for zero/near-zero, buckets 1-3 the three warm steps below — and a small "Less → More" key repeats the same 4 swatches so the mapping is legible without hovering every cell.

data array<{label,value}> [{"label":"Day 1","value":4}, {"label":"Day 2","value":10}, … 28 days total] one cell per item; value's share of the series max picks one of four discrete buckets — never a continuous mix
columns number 7 grid-template-columns count — 7 reads as a calendar week

2026-08-13 — this entry previously described a retired mechanism (a per-cell `color-mix()` toward `hsl(var(--muted))`, scaled continuously by value, with a `color` prop to pick the mix's full-strength end). That is gone; four fixed buckets have nothing left for a caller to retint, so `color` is gone with it. Bucket 1-3's three hex values (#FFD9BF/#FF9E5E/#F25A00) are written literally, not through a token — DataCharts.jsx's file banner names this its one deliberate exception to "nothing here writes a hex": a legend of four literal swatches can always be pointed at, where a formula's output can't. Bucket 0 stays a real token, `--color-track` — the same resting-groove role HBars' and GaugeRing's tracks read.

Same label · track · fill row as HBars, except the track holds several segments instead of one, each keyed by `keys[].key` and sized to its share of the row's total. A legend below the rows repeats each key's swatch and label, same colour resolution as the segments.

No per-segment radius. The track owns the shape: `rounded-bar` + `overflow-hidden` on the track clips the first and last segments to whatever the active language's bar radius is. The old version hard-coded `first:rounded-l-full last:rounded-r-full` — Beacon's 999px pill, and nobody else's. Same flex-line correction as FunnelChart's row, and this one had it worse: the label used to carry no `min-w-label`/`max-w-label` at all, so its width was purely the grid's hard-coded 7rem.

<Donut · Legend/>

A composition ring, and the key beside it.

kit/Donut.jsx

[SOURCE] Donut.dc.html (Claude Design project "Mobile app style guide sheet"). The groove is stroke-track — the same token every bar's trough and GaugeRing's own groove read. Segments walk --chart-1..6 — SIX steps, not eight, per tokens.css's own chart-ramp note — the same ramp DataCharts.dc.html names, so a legend beside a bar chart and a legend beside a donut on the same screen agree because both read the same six tokens, not because they happen to match today. A per-datum color always wins over the ramp; that's also the entire de-emphasis-walk mechanism below — no separate prop for it.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
segments array<{key,label,value,color?}> [{ key: "approved", label: "Approved", value: 311 }, …] proportioned against their OWN total — a per-datum color wins over the ramp; that's also how the de-emphasis walk works, no separate prop
size "sm" | "md" | "lg" "lg" 84/9 · 120/12 · 172/15 (box px / stroke px). Thickness scales with the ring, never independently — no separate thickness prop anymore
activeIndex number | null 0 controlled, not internal state — thickens + focuses that segment, fades the rest to 35%, swaps the center figure to that segment's own value/label. Wire it to Legend's onActiveChange
caption string "total" resting caption under the figure; swaps to the active segment's own label on hover
sublabel string "380" overrides the resting figure — defaults to the computed total
label string "Claims by outcome" caption below the ring, and the aria-label when there is no data
items array<{key,label,value?,color?}> [{ key: "approved", label: "Approved", value: 311 }, …] Legend's own list — same shape as segments, usually the same array
showValue boolean true prints the count in the data voice beside each swatch
showPercent boolean true right-aligned, fixed-width column, against the items' own total

[OURS]: drawing each slice as one dashed <circle> with a rotate transform rather than building it as an arc path — cheaper, rounder, and it keeps a slice one element so a hover title lands on the whole thing rather than half of it. Caps are strokeLinecap="butt", stated explicitly now — round caps and gaps both misread the last slice's size. NEW: the legend is the interactive surface, not the ring — hovering a row thickens that arc (stroke width steps up per size), fades the rest to 35% opacity, and swaps the center figure to that row's own value + label; the ring never reacts to its own hover, so activeIndex is a controlled pair lifted to the caller (see the second specimen, pinned on "Approved" since a static snippet has no hover state of its own). Legend's dot is size-2 (8px) now, one step up from chip-dot (7px), since it labels a thicker arc than a status chip labels a status.

<Table/>

A real <table>, so a screen reader announces the column a cell belongs to.

kit/Tables.jsx

Columns and rows, with the language's own header band, row rule, density and mono voice. Four row states at two different weights: hover and selection are half-strength washes, a row's own tone is full-strength and always wins — a selected, hovered claim that failed still reads as failed.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
columns array<{key,label,align?,mono?,width?,sortable?}> [{ key: "ref", label: "Ref", mono: true, width: "8.5rem" }, …] align:"right" pairs with tabular numerals; mono is the data voice — refs, IDs, dates; sortable renders that header as a chevron button
rows array<{…keyed by column.key}> { ref: "CLM-4417", title: "Compressor seal failure", owner: "R. Iyer", days: 12 } a cell value may be a node — a status column drops a <StatusChip/> straight in
onRowClick (row, i) => void — supplying it makes rows hoverable (bg-row-hover) and clickable; omit and they're inert
rowKey (row, i) => string (r) => r.ref stable key — also what selection is keyed by, so it has to identify a row, not its position
selected / onSelect key[] / (nextKeys) => void ["CLM-4419"] adds the checkbox column; onSelect receives the whole NEXT array — Table never owns selection itself
sort / onSort {key,dir} / (key) => void { key: "days", dir: "desc" } sort is display-only, Table doesn't reorder rows; onSort fires when a sortable header is clicked
rowTone (row) => tone (r) => r.tone === "danger" ? "danger" : undefined tints a row at full strength (success/warning/info/danger) — always wins over hover and selection
compact boolean true the one density knob — 10px cell padding instead of 13px, table-wide
empty string "No claims match this filter." shown instead of an empty table when rows.length is 0

markup 
<p class="m-0 py-6 text-center text-sm text-text-muted">No claims match this filter.</p>

A row rule is not the same colour as a panel's own edge — Beacon draws rows one step quieter than a container border, which is why the rule reads border-gray-1 rather than border-border. The header band's near-white fill is not a new literal either: bg-row-hover already resolves to that exact value, so the band reuses it instead of minting a second token for the same colour.

<StatTile/>

A label, a figure and an optional unit — plus, when the number has a history, a tone pill and a spark.

kit/Cards.jsx

DEFAULT TO THE FIRST SPECIMEN BELOW (delta + spark), not the second. A page agent computing a KPI row from real seed data almost always HAS a history to show — a count grouped by date, a level checked against a threshold across recent readings, a status derived from a date range — even when no field is literally named "history". Reach for the second, bare specimen only when a metric truly has no computable historical dimension anywhere in the seed (e.g. a first-run empty state), never as the default shape for "a row of KPI tiles". This is the one component in the cookbook where copying the FIRST matching example verbatim (the cookbook's own house rule) has repeatedly produced bare tiles across unrelated apps because the bare specimen used to sort first — fixed by reordering, but the underlying judgment call is the page agent's: derive a real series, don't reach for the shortcut. [SOURCE] in Beacon — a label, a 32px Poppins figure with tabular numerals ("Tabular numerals so columns align"), and a unit on the baseline. The tile itself is [OURS]: the source names the TYPE but pairs it with no container. It sits on a metric-role card, which is exactly what card-pad-metric was named for. The delta pill and the sparkline are [OURS] and both are OPTIONAL — pass neither and this is the plain tile it has always been, byte for byte. They were briefly drafted as a second component and folded back in, because the split could not be defended: a KPI tile that shows its trend is not a different component from one that does not, it is the same tile with more to say. Two entries would have meant two specimens to keep in step, two names for a page agent to choose between on a distinction the reader never sees, and a second card anatomy free to drift from this one.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
label string "Open claims" caption above the figure, in text-kpi-label
value node "42" the figure itself — tabular numerals so a row of tiles aligns column-wise
unit string "this month" sits on the figure's baseline, in the muted meta ink
alarm boolean true recolours the FIGURE to --primary — an attention state on the number, not a badge beside it
delta string "−2 wk" OPTIONAL. A tinted pill at the top right, attached to the label rather than trailing the figure. Text, not a number: it carries its own period, so "−2 wk" and "1 closed" are both legal
tone "success" · "danger" · "warning" · "info" "danger" OPTIONAL. Colours the pill, the spark and the figure together, uniformly — one state. Passed, not derived from the delta's sign — see the footer
deltaTone "success" · "danger" · "warning" · "info" "success" OPTIONAL, falls back to tone. Lets the PILL diverge from tone/figure/spark — three independent colours a single tone can't express (a green pill, a plain dark figure, the language's own default spark). This is what the first specimen row demonstrates.
series array<number> [8, 9, 7, 10, 9, 12, 10] OPTIONAL. Draws the filled area spark along the card's foot. 2+ points renders one; omit it and the card draws no spark at all, StatTile's own behaviour for a metric with no history yet

DEFAULT — delta + series: deltaTone lets the pill read independently of the figure and the spark

<div class="grid gap-3.5 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-4">
  <section class="bg-surface shadow-panel text-secondary rounded-xl card-pad-metric">
    <div class="flex items-start justify-between gap-3">
      <p class="m-0 min-w-0 truncate text-kpi-label text-text-muted">System uptime</p>
      <span class="flex-none rounded-full px-2 py-0.5 font-mono text-data font-semibold tabular-nums bg-success-bg text-success-ink">+0.1</span>
    </div>
    <p class="m-0 flex items-baseline gap-2" style="margin-top: var(--kpi-gap, 12px)">
      <span class="font-display text-[28px] font-medium tracking-[-.028em] tabular-nums leading-none text-secondary">99.9</span>
      <span class="text-kpi-label text-text-subtle">%</span>
    </p>

alarm recolours the FIGURE, not a badge beside it — Beacon's own behaviour, where an overdue count turns primary-strong. That is a state on the number, which is why there is no icon slot here; when a card needs a category chip as well, that is MetricCard. TONE IS THE CLAIM, and it is passed rather than derived from the delta's sign: a rising overdue count and a rising completion rate are opposite news, so no rule about + and − can get both right. It colours the pill AND the spark together, both from --tone-*-fg, so a card cannot disagree with itself; omit it and both fall back to the accent, which is the honest rendering for a figure that is simply moving. tone also supersedes alarm on the figure when both are given — alarm says "look at this", tone says what kind of news it is, and the more specific statement wins. The spark is the shell's own .kit-spark, which existed and was drawn by nothing — no catalog entry referenced it, so no page agent knew it was there. 2026-08-13, later still — found by a sibling agent auditing the prototype against this entry: the wrapper and the spark had both drifted independently of the delta-pill fix above. Cards.jsx's own redesign (found and fixed elsewhere in this catalog the same day) moved every Card anatomy — including StatTile's own `<Card role="metric">` wrapper — off `shadow-card bg-card text-card-foreground` onto `shadow-panel bg-surface text-secondary`; this entry never got that follow-up. Separately, `.kit-spark`'s shared-CSS-class mechanism described above is itself now stale: the real `Spark` (Cards.jsx, unexported, StatTile's own anatomy) draws a REAL per-instance `<linearGradient>` (opacity .22→0, `useId()`-keyed so multiple tiles never collide on one `<defs>` id) rather than colouring a shared class via CSS — `.kit-spark`'s tone modifiers (`.warning` etc.) don't exist in the real component at all. Rewritten below to match exactly.

<MetricCard/>

StatTile's richer sibling — an icon chip, the figure, and a trend line.

kit/Compat.jsx

The same metric-role card StatTile draws, with two things StatTile deliberately refuses. That refusal is on the record in kit/Cards.jsx and in StatTile's own footer here, in the same words: alarm recolours the FIGURE, "which is why there is no icon slot here". So the anatomy went where the props already were — MetricCard has always ACCEPTED icon and delta, it simply rendered the icon as inline text beside the label. Two components, two answers, both stated. Reach for StatTile when the number is the whole story and MetricCard when it needs a category and a direction.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
icon node <svg width="16" height="16">…</svg> rides in an --accent chip at the card's rounded-lg rung; omit it and the figure takes the full width, which is StatTile
label string "Open claims" caption above the figure, in text-kpi-label, truncating rather than wrapping
value node "42" the figure — tabular numerals so a row of tiles aligns column-wise
sub string "this month" sits on the figure's baseline, in the muted meta ink
delta number 12 signed. Success above zero, danger below; exactly zero renders NOTHING rather than a flat 0%
deltaLabel string "vs last month" what the delta is measured against — without it a percentage is a number with no claim attached
tone tone name "indigo" colours the figure through the legacy tone names, which resolve to the language's own chart ramp
spark / featured any — accepted and DROPPED rather than faked — no language declares a KPI sparkline, and one drawn in an un-themed colour is worse than none

a row of four — three with an icon chip, two with a trend, one with neither. The fourth is what StatTile draws.

The chip's RADIUS is the contract's and its SIZE is not: `rounded-lg` is the "a surface inside a surface steps down one rung" token Card's nested specimen reads, and a chip on a card is exactly that; 44px is stock Tailwind, the same way KanbanBoard's column width and FunnelChart's bar height are. Colour, radius, shadow and type come from the contract — structural lengths do not have to. The fill is --accent, the tint every language already keeps for a quiet inset, because no language declares a KPI icon tile at all. THE TREND ARROW IS DRAWN, NOT TYPED: a ▲ character inherits the font and shifts its weight and baseline across Poppins, Archivo and Manrope, where an SVG triangle sits identically in all three — Breadcrumb's argument for its separator, and it wins here for the same reason. One path, rotated 180° for a fall, so the two directions cannot drift apart. A delta of exactly zero renders nothing rather than a flat 0%, and the arrow is aria-hidden with the direction carried on the label instead, so a screen reader hears "up 12 percent" rather than "12%".

<Calendar · Agenda/>

A month grid with event markers, and the dated list that reads beside it.

kit/Calendar.jsx

[OURS], no design language declares a calendar — every value below is still a token tokens.css already holds: the row hover, the grid rule, the tone map, the data voice. TWO components, not one, sharing a data shape and nothing else: the old cookbook fused a month grid and an upcoming rail into a single 12-column block, which meant neither could be used alone — a page that wants only "what is next" had to render a month it did not need.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
days number 31 how many cells the month has — the caller's fact, not computed
lead number 4 blank cells before day 1. Which weekday the month starts on is a fact about that month in that year.
events array<{day,title,time,tone,kind}> { day: 18, title: "Survey — MV Northern Compass", tone: "danger", kind: "Survey" } marks a day with up to three tone dots; Agenda reads the same array
selected / onSelect number / fn 18 supplying onSelect makes cells real buttons, and only on MARKED days — an empty day is not a target. Omit it and the grid is inert
today number 12 a 1px inset ring, not a fill — stacks with Selected instead of competing with it
title / lead string / number "Upcoming" / 4 Agenda: caller-supplied facts it cannot derive — title because Agenda has no month/year context, lead because a row's weekday abbreviation needs to know where day 1 sat
day number 18 Agenda: filters to one day. Omit it and every event lists, day-ascending
onSelect / onClear fn / fn — Agenda: onSelect makes rows clickable; onClear renders the "Whole month" pill, shown only once a day is set

Calendar — events + onSelect: August, day 18 selected, day 12 is today

DATES ARE STRINGS AND NUMBERS, never Date objects. A prototype's SEED is JSON and a Kissflow date field arrives as an ISO string; parsing to a Date and back is exactly where timezone drift enters a component that has no business knowing about timezones. So `day` is the number printed in the cell, and nothing here computes one from the other — including `lead`, the count of blank cells before day 1 (Agenda's own weekday abbreviation needs that same fact, which is why it takes `lead` too). Leading AND trailing blanks now render, so the grid always completes to full rows. A marked day draws at most THREE dots however many events it holds: a cell is not a legend. Today is a 1px INSET ring, not a fill, so it survives sitting on a Selected cell instead of competing with it — Selected itself is a fill (--color-primary-bg / -primary-ink), which is also why a selected day's dots recolour to -primary-ink: a coloured dot on a coloured fill is illegible. A day is a real target only when it is BOTH marked and `onSelect` is supplied — "an empty day is not a target." Agenda's spine reads the SAME token as the day's own dot, so the grid and the list key together by construction, not by two authors agreeing today.

<ProgressBar · SegmentBar · ProgressList/>

One rail, reused three ways: bare, split proportionally, or listed with labels.

kit/Progress.jsx

A progress rail and a chart bar are the same object, so they share the track token — bg-track — everywhere. The height doesn't have to match: this page draws it at h-1.5 (6px), DataCharts' own bars at h-2.5 (10px). One token, two heights, on purpose. The fill is --color-primary unset, or a tone's own -dot value with it (the solid dot value, "exactly where a tone's full strength is allowed to appear") — a caller-supplied tone, never derived from the number itself.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
value number 68 ProgressBar: a percentage unless max is given
max number 100 ProgressBar: value is read against this, not against the largest value in a set
tone enum "danger" ProgressBar: unset takes --color-primary
label string "Marine" ProgressBar: adds the label column at min-w-22, truncating rather than wrapping
showValue boolean true ProgressBar/ProgressList: appends the percentage in the data voice
indeterminate boolean true ProgressBar: a fixed ~34% fill in --color-border; no percentage announced — aria-valuenow is omitted, not sent as 0
segments array<{key,label,value,color?}> [{ key: "approved", label: "Approved", value: 311 }, …] SegmentBar: proportioned within the row, not against 100. A zero-value segment is skipped, not a zero-width sliver
legend boolean true SegmentBar: the key below, with counts in the data voice
items array<{label,value,max?,tone?}> [{ label: "Marine", value: 92 }, { label: "Energy", value: 12, tone: "danger" }] ProgressList: each row scaled against its OWN max, not the largest value in the set

        <span class="absolute inset-y-0 left-0 rounded-full bg-danger transition-[width] duration-[160ms] ease-standard" style="width: 12%"></span>
      </span>
      <span class="min-w-value text-right font-mono text-data tabular-nums text-secondary">12%</span>
    </div>
  </li>
</ul>

ProgressList is not HBars wearing a different name, though it looks like one. HBars scales every row against the largest VALUE in the set, so its longest bar always reaches the end of its track; ProgressList scales each row against its own MAX, so a row at 40% looks like 40% regardless of what the others do. Using HBars for completion figures is the classic way to make three-quarters done look finished. indeterminate is a fixed ~34%-wide fill in --color-border, not a tone and not primary — there is no known value to colour toward — and sends no aria-valuenow at all rather than a dishonest 0 or the fixed 34. [OURS]: the fill below reads as a literal bg-<tone>-dot/bg-primary/bg-border CLASS, not Progress.jsx's own inline `style="background: var(--color-<tone>-dot, var(--color-<tone>-ink))"` — this session's StatTile fix found every -bg AND -dot tone token empty through a raw var() in this catalog's runtime (checked systematically; only -fg/-ink tokens resolve), so the same class-based fix applies here. danger has no --color-danger-dot token to begin with ("dot reuses --color-danger, per Foundations"), so its fill reads bg-danger directly, same as Calendar's event dots do.

Controls #cat-controls

<Button/>

One action, at one of four ranks — primary, secondary, outline, strong.

kit/Buttons.jsx

FOUR ranks, still not "as many as you like" — Buttons.jsx's own words, and rank stays a CLOSED SET: these snippets are the whole vocabulary, not a sample of it. REDESIGNED 2026-08-13 off Buttons.dc.html (the page after Cards.dc.html in the same Claude Design migration): primary now carries its own gradient glow (`--gradient-primary` / `--shadow-primary`) instead of a flat fill, secondary is a white `--shadow-contact` fill instead of a gray one, and outline is the only rank with a border — transparent until hovered, for a dismiss beside a commit. Button is also the only control in this catalog that renders a focus ring, and the ring is the contract's one deliberate bypass of the HSL-triplet convention: `--color-ring` is `rgba(255, 98, 3, .35)`, a whole alpha value with nowhere to put that alpha inside an HSL triplet. It sits 2px OFF the button's own edge on a transparent offset (new in this pass) so it shows whatever is actually behind the button instead of painting a fake white halo on a gray or dark surface. Tab through the first specimen to see it.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
rank enum "strong" primary · secondary · outline · strong — picks the fill. Closed set, no fifth.
size enum "form" sm · header · form · mobile · icon · icon-sm — geometry only, off Tailwind's own scale. header is the default.
tone enum "danger" only "danger" exists — swaps in primary's shape with --color-danger's fill. Exclusive with rank; reserved for a confirm dialog.
loading boolean true an inline spinner before the label. Presentational only — pass disabled too if clicks should stop.
action string "submitClaim" the handler the click fires — never inferred from the label text
label string "Submit claim" the button's own text, set by the caller, not derived from action
disabled boolean true driven by a domain condition (claim.status !== "draft") — an already-approved claim can't be resubmitted

the four ranks — primary, secondary, outline, strong

Geometry is a `size`, not a token bundle any more — the old `control-shape`/`rounded-control-strong` bundles are retired, replaced by four literal Tailwind sizes (`sm` · `header` · `form` · `mobile`) plus two icon sizes that break the pill on purpose ("a round icon button reads as an avatar" — 36px `--radius-md` in a top bar, 28px `--radius-sm` inside a row). `header` is the default, at 34px — down from the old control-shape's 42px, a visible height drop across every existing call site, not a per-call-site opt-in. `strong` is still the only rank carrying `shadow-button` — Foundations' own "black buttons only" role, so the create action reads as the nearest object. `tone="danger"` is NOT a fifth rank: it always renders primary's shape (pill, white ink, no border) with `--color-danger`'s fill, exclusive with `rank` rather than layered on it, reserved for a confirm dialog. `loading` is purely presentational — an inline spinner shown BEFORE the label, replacing nothing, that does not imply `disabled` on its own. Four ranks is a closed set — do not invent a fifth.

<Input · Select · Textarea/>

The three text-entry controls, sharing one field geometry and one focus contract.

kit/Fields.jsx

ONE Entry for three components, because kit/Fields.jsx is one file for a reason: Input and Select read the exported `FIELD` class string VERBATIM, so their height, ink and focus behaviour are a SINGLE decision, not three coincidentally similar ones — SearchBar (kit/Fx.jsx) reads the identical string too. Splitting Input/Select/Textarea into three Entries here would invent a distinction the source does not make. RETUNED 2026-08-13 off Fields.dc.html (the page after Buttons.dc.html in the same Claude Design migration), its own token-mapping table: "10px corners, a softer edge, and a 3px ring instead of 2". Box radius moved to --radius-md (10px, was 8px), the resting edge to --color-gray-3 (was --color-border), and focus now puts a 3px --color-ring halo at offset 0 around a --color-primary edge. Hover is NEW — a --color-text-subtle edge, a state this control never had before. Textarea is [OURS]: no page declares a multi-line field, so its min-height (132px) is the box's own new 44px height times three, not the old 138px composed off the retired 46px number.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
claim.reference string "WC-2026-0143" Input value — a system-issued reference, usually shown disabled
claim.department enum "Marine" Select's bound field; the option list mirrors the model's picklist — Marine · Aviation · Rail · Energy
claim.status enum "review" Select, pre-selected — open · review · closed
claim.findings string "Compressor seal failed under load." Textarea value — free text, no length cap in the model

Geometry is no longer a token bundle. `field-shape`/`field-multiline`, the @utility pair FIELD used to compose, are DROPPED here — the same move Buttons.jsx made retiring `control-shape`: literal Tailwind geometry (`h-11 px-3.5`) over a token-driven bundle. Both utilities stay UNCHANGED in tokens.css at their old 46px fallback, since Command.jsx and FlowViews.jsx still read `field-shape` directly — a real, visible divergence (44px here, 46px there) flagged for its own follow-up pass, not fixed by this entry. Select's chevron is a background image, not a sibling element, so the control stays one focusable box — a wrapper with an absolutely-positioned icon would put the ring around the wrapper instead of the field, which is the exact failure `appearance-none` plus a background image avoids. That chevron is also the one value in these three controls that does NOT move with a future retint: its stroke is baked into the data URI as `%23656e7a` — Beacon's own ink, frozen at that literal — because a background-image has no access to the host document's cascade and so cannot read currentColor or any token. Transcribed as-is rather than fixed, because inventing a token-driven chevron is markup the source itself doesn't ship.

<SearchBar · FilterBar/>

The two things that sit above a list — and they are not the same thing.

kit/Fx.jsx

ONE entry for both, because the difference only reads when you see them together. FilterBar is a CLOSED set: four pills, one active, the whole vocabulary visible at once. SearchBar is OPEN — free text against a corpus nobody has enumerated, plus dropdowns whose options come from the data. They sit in the same place on a page and are read completely differently, so merging them would produce one component whose shape depends on a prop. SearchBar is the old cookbook's "Search + filter bar" recipe; FilterBar existed only in the starter kit. Both are now on both sides.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
query string "" SearchBar's bound text. `placeholder` doubles as the input's aria-label — a search box with no visible label still needs a name.
selects[] array<{label,value,options}> { label: "Department", options: ["Marine","Aviation","Rail","Energy"] } each narrower renders at the same field geometry; options take strings or {value,label}
count string "42 results" right-aligned, in the data voice. Omit it and nothing takes that space — never render "0 results" before a search has run.
filters[] array<{value,label,count?}> [{ value: "open", label: "Open", count: 42 }, …] FilterBar's closed set. A bare string is accepted as its own label; the count rides INSIDE the pill so a filter stays one target.

SearchBar's input and its selects wear kit/Fields.jsx's exported FIELD class string VERBATIM, so a search box and a form input are the same height, radius, fill and focus ring — a search box one pixel off every other input is the classic way a shared design system stops being shared, and a duplicated class string is how it happens. The magnifier is a positioned SIBLING with pl-9 clearing it, NOT a background image: a background image is the trick Select uses, and it is the one thing about Select that does not follow the language, because a data URI cannot read the host cascade and its chevron is frozen at Beacon's ink. A real element inherits currentColor and moves. FilterBar borrows TabStrip's geometry so a filter row and a tab row are the same height everywhere, but it carries no role="tab" — a filter is a control, not navigation.

<TabStrip/>

A segmented control — pill tabs, one active fill shared with Button's fourth rank.

kit/TabStrip.jsx

Named TabStrip, not Tabs, because `kf/Tabs.jsx` is the legacy component and stays exported until the old bench goes — same reason ModelChart sits beside Chart. REDESIGNED 2026-08-13 off TabStrip.dc.html (the page right after Buttons.dc.html in the same Claude Design migration), [SOURCE] drawn directly from its own words: "a segmented control... near-black active pill, plain inactive label, nothing else."

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
claim.status enum "review" the bound field — its value picks which tab renders active
items[].badge number 42 optional count, rides inside the tab; omit it for a plain segmented control
track boolean true wraps the strip in a --color-gray-1 pill and drops each tab from 40px to 34px — for a tab group that sits on a white card and needs its own edge

The active fill and its hover are `--color-secondary` and `--color-secondary-hover` EXACTLY — the same pair Buttons.jsx's `strong` rank reads (`bg-secondary` / `hover:bg-secondary-hover`), confirmed against Buttons.jsx directly rather than approximated. Not a coincidence to tidy away: a black tab and a strong button are the same black, and a tab-only colour token would let the two drift apart under a retune the source says they move together on. Geometry is two literal Tailwind sizes now, not a token bundle — the same move Buttons.jsx made retiring `control-shape` — and they land exactly on Buttons.jsx's own `form` (h-10, text-sm) and `header` (h-[34px], text-xs) geometry, so a tab and its nearest button size agree on type scale, not just height. Inactive hover goes to FULL ink (`text-secondary`), not a lighter shade of muted — the same step a secondary button takes under the cursor. The badge count rides INSIDE the tab rather than beside it, so a tab stays one target, and it takes the mono voice; it does NOT follow the label's hover step, staying `--color-text-muted` regardless, so it needs its own explicit colour class rather than inheriting the label's ink.

<Checkbox · Switch/>

The two boolean controls — one a form field, one an instant setting.

kit/Fields.jsx

ONE Entry because they share a contract in the source: both are hand-rolled in kit/Fields.jsx around the same `has-[:focus-visible]:ring` wrapper, so the focus story is a single decision rather than two coincidentally similar ones. They are NOT interchangeable, and the difference is intent rather than shape: a Checkbox is a FIELD — it takes a value that is submitted with the rest of a form and means nothing until the form is saved. A Switch is a SETTING — it acts the moment it moves, and there is no Save button waiting for it. Pick by what happens on click, never by which one looks better in the row.

disabled boolean false a domain condition, not a style choice — adds cursor-not-allowed + opacity-60

<Label/>

The caption above a field.

kit/Fields.jsx

Its own Entry rather than folded into `fields`, and the reason is the same one that keeps Input, Select and Textarea together: `fields` is one entry because those three literally share the `FIELD` class string in the source. Label shares nothing with them — it is `text-xs font-semibold text-text-muted` and stops there. It exists for a caption `Field`'s own built-in label doesn't fit: beside a Checkbox or Switch, or captioning a custom composite that isn't one of the three fields in that file. Grouping it into `fields` would invent a shared decision the component does not make.

The input is `border-0 bg-transparent` on purpose — the palette's surface is the panel, so a field edge inside it would draw a box inside a box; the border-bottom under the search row does the work a border would, at one weight instead of two. Rows read ONE selected state — `data-[selected=true]:bg-primary-bg data-[selected=true]:text-primary-ink`, the SAME pair the selected nav item uses — because cmdk's own `data-[selected=true]` already fires for both pointer hover and keyboard focus: "the pointer moves the same cursor the arrow keys do, so the two can never disagree about which row Enter will open." That's the one place this differs from DropdownMenuItem, which still carries an independent `data-[highlighted]:bg-gray-1` hover of its own. CommandFooter is NEW — a key-hint bar (white keycap pills on a `--color-row-hover` wash) with a live result count on the right; omitting it in a palette with one group is the caller's call, not something this entry decides for you.

REDESIGNED 2026-08-13 off Floating.dc.html, [OURS] throughout (the spec names no dedicated "DropdownMenu" component, only the shared surface recipe). It shares its surface exactly with Popover — `border-decor border-gray-2 shadow-overlay rounded-lg bg-surface text-secondary` — because a menu and a popover are the SAME object (content floating near where you asked for it) doing two jobs, and giving them two surfaces would say they are two things. What differs is padding: `p-1` here for a dense item list, `p-4` on Popover for free-form content. Items are `rounded-sm` (6px, Foundations' own "small marks" radius), one rung tighter than the panel's `rounded-lg`, so a highlighted row sits inside the corner instead of fighting it. Highlighted reads `--color-gray-1` — pointer hover AND keyboard focus are the SAME state, Radix's own `data-[highlighted]` firing for both — except a `destructive` item, which swaps that wash for the `--color-danger-bg` TINT (never the solid `--color-danger` fill) and its own text to `--color-danger-ink`, composed as exactly ONE `data-[highlighted]:bg-*` per item instance so two same-specificity utilities never land on the same element.

Surfaces #cat-surfaces

<Card/>

The surface. role picks the padding for its content; tone tints the whole tile and drops the shadow.

kit/Cards.jsx

[SOURCE] Cards.dc.html, and the component its own padding ladder was transcribed for: metric 20 / list 24 / doc 28, one role per kind of content — "KPI and figure tiles", "list and table cards", "long-form and documentation cards". No border on any panel any more, at any role: separation is `--shadow-panel` alone. 2026-08-13 — every specimen's own title reproduces CardTitle's markup, not a bare <h3>, so this stays in lockstep with kit/Cards.jsx by construction: text-[15px] → text-lg, on request (found live, DamWatch, reading as an afterthought beside a 22px gauge figure).

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
role enum "doc" "metric" · "list" · "doc" — 20 / 24 / 28px, Cards.dc.html's own three. Defaults to "list".
tone enum "primary" primary · success · warning · danger · info · neutral — tints the whole surface from that tone's -bg/-ink pair and drops --shadow-panel. neutral (or no tone) renders the plain white panel with its shadow instead.
clickable boolean true Opt-in. No edge left to warm any more, so the whole hover response is --shadow-panel deepening to --shadow-raised with a 2px lift.
nested boolean true A surface inside another surface: drops to a --color-gray-1 fill at --radius-lg instead of stacking a second shadow.

the three padding roles

metric — 20px

Dense. The number carries the card.

list — 24px

Rows bring their own rhythm.

doc — 28px

Long-form text needs the air.

    gray fill instead — visible on its own, and the only thing separating it from the white doc card
    holding it.
  </p>
</section>

One surface, one way to separate it from `--color-canvas`: `--shadow-panel` — a 1px contact layer plus a soft, wide lift — at `--radius-xl`. Nest a card inside another and it drops that shadow for a flat `--color-gray-1` fill at the tighter `--radius-lg` instead, so two panels never stack the same lift twice. Give it a tone and it drops the shadow for the same reason — a tinted fill already separates itself from the canvas; `neutral` (or no tone) keeps the plain white panel and its shadow, because gray-on-canvas has no fill to read. Only `clickable` puts the shadow back to work, deepening it to `--shadow-raised` with a 2px lift on hover — there is no border left to warm any more.

<PhotoCard/>

A directory tile for a thing you can photograph — and the honest alternative when you cannot.

kit/Cards.jsx

The old cookbook's "Directory photo-card", now a component on both sides. It is the ONE place in either kit that renders an image, and that is why it is its own export rather than a Card variant: a photograph is a surface no design language governs. Its colours are the picture's, not the theme's, so it has to be fenced — a fixed-height, overflow-hidden band at the top of the card, with everything below it back under the contract.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
image / alt string "…/vessel.jpg" the only <img> in the kit. Fenced into a fixed-height, overflow-hidden band: a photograph's colours are its own, not the theme's.
icon node <svg …> the other half of the component, NOT a fallback. Abstract entities — a GL account, a policy — have no photograph, and stock imagery for one turns a directory of abstractions into a stock-photo catalogue.
title / meta string "MV Northern Compass" / "Bulk carrier · Singapore" both truncate; a directory grid whose tiles are different heights is a directory nobody scans
badge node <StatusChip tone="warning">Survey due</StatusChip> sits over the band's top-right corner, usually a StatusChip
stat {label,value,percent} { label: "Utilisation", value: "86%", percent: 86 } a labelled figure, plus the bar if percent is given. Reads the same h-bar/rounded-bar/bg-track geometry every other bar in the kit does.
onClick () => void () => {} makes the whole card clickable through Card's own hover contract

THE ICON VARIANT IS NOT A FALLBACK, it is the other half of the component, and the cookbook said so first: photographs belong to photographable entities — a vessel, a building, a person. A GL account, a policy, a config record has no photograph, and inventing stock imagery for one is how a directory of abstractions ends up looking like a stock-photo catalogue. NO SPECIMEN BELOW LOADS A PICTURE, on the same rule CustomEmbed states outright: a catalog page should not reach the network. It is also why the empty band reads `bg-track` and not `bg-gray-1` — a photo that hasn't loaded is a groove waiting to be filled, the same role a chart's own track plays, not a generic quiet fill (that is Skeleton's role, and Skeleton reads `bg-gray-1` for exactly that reason). The card takes Card's `bare` role — no padding at all — because its first child bleeds to the card's own corners; the body below supplies `card-pad-list` itself.

<Callout/>

A full-width tinted message. Same tone map as the chip, at a card's density.

kit/Callout.jsx

[SOURCE] Callout.dc.html — composed, not transcribed, and it says so itself: "the style guide declares no callout... but every value is a token something else already declares." The tone map is StatusChip's, the padding/radius ladder is Cards'. If Foundations ever draws a callout directly, expect the geometry to move and the palette not to. NO NEUTRAL TONE: "a gray tinted box on a white card is just a card, so use one" — a Callout that wants to be neutral should be a Card instead.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
tone enum "danger" "success" | "warning" | "info" | "danger" — four, not five. Default "info".
title string "Rejected" bold first line. Optional — a one-line callout usually needs none.
onDismiss () => void () => {} supplying it renders the close control
icon node <svg …> replaces the dot entirely at size-4, drawn in currentColor. Never both together.
compact boolean true p-4 · --radius-md instead of p-6 · --radius-lg — for inside a form or card

every tone — the dot is the chip's own dot, at the callout's scale

One deliberate exception to the rest of the language: every tone here keeps a 1px edge in its own `--color-<tone>-dot`, always — "the tint alone is too quiet on a white page." Nowhere else in Beacon draws a border any more; this is the one surface that still needs one. `color` is set once, on the outer element, to the tone's ink — title, body and the dismiss button all inherit it via `currentColor` rather than each re-declaring a text colour. `icon` REPLACES the dot entirely when passed, never both at once.

<Modal/>

A dialog over the page. Traps focus, locks scroll, and returns focus to its trigger on close.

kit/Overlay.jsx

[SOURCE] Overlay.dc.html: a dialog centred over a `--color-scrim`, `--radius-lg` and `--shadow-overlay`, no border. It traps focus, locks the page behind it from scrolling, and hands focus back to whatever opened it on close.

width string "34rem" capped at 100%

open it — Escape, the scrim, and the close button all dismiss

No border: the source doc states it outright — "no border on a modal; a sheet takes one on its inner edge" — so the panel is `shadow-overlay` alone. The destructive action in a confirm dialog is the one place a tone appears at full strength on a button — `--color-danger`, solid, not the tint — "because the tint would read as a status rather than an action." That's Buttons.jsx's `tone="danger"`, reached for here in the footer with dismiss to its left.

<PageHeader/>

Breadcrumb, title, optional subtitle, optional actions, optional stat row.

kit/Layout.jsx

The least token-hungry components in the set, and that is the point of writing them down: a layout primitive should consume spacing and nothing else. No language declares a page header, and none should — a column count or a title size is not a design-language decision. `breadcrumb` is a slot, not a rendered Breadcrumb, so PageHeader doesn't couple to that file's own in-flight migration.

subtitle string "Every claim raised in the last 90 days…" capped at 2xl so a long one wraps rather than spanning the page
actions node <Button rank="strong">New claim</Button> right-aligned, wraps below on narrow viewports. At most one primary.

`cols` is a MAXIMUM, not a fixed count — 1 below sm, 2 below lg, then `cols` — and the responsive steps are hard-coded rather than accepted as a prop, so every grid in the app breaks at the same two places, which is what makes a page read as one page. `Split`'s rail is `lg:` only; below that it stacks BELOW the main content rather than above it, because a rail is secondary by definition. `Bento` admits exactly three spans (`2x1` · `1x2` · `2x2`) — a bento with arbitrary spans stops being a layout and becomes a canvas.

An empty state is NOT an error. It takes the muted ink and no tone, because tinting it turns "no rows yet" into "something is wrong". Only NoAccess carries a tone, and a quiet one — a permission boundary is a fact about the viewer, not a failure. NoAccess stays separate from EmptyState rather than becoming a tone of it, because merging them produces an empty state with a Create button the viewer cannot use. Skeleton reads `--color-gray-1`, Feedback.dc.html's own mapping for the skeleton fill — not `bg-track`, which is a different role (the groove under a rail, bar or gauge) that only happens to be a similar grey.

<Sheet/>

A panel that slides in from an edge — a Modal with more room.

kit/Overlay.jsx

The same job as Modal at a different scale. The choice between them is about the TASK, not the amount of text: a Modal interrupts — it centres itself and asks one question you answer before continuing. A Sheet accompanies — it takes an edge and lets the page stay legible beside it, which is what a multi-field create/edit form needs, because you want the record you were looking at to still be there.

open / onClose boolean / () => void () => {} controlled, exactly like Modal
side enum "right" left · right — which edge it enters from. Right is the default for detail/edit; left reads as navigation.
width string "26rem" capped at 100% so it becomes full-bleed on a phone rather than overflowing
title / footer node "Edit request" same slots as Modal — the footer is where the actions go

It shares Modal's focus-trap and scroll-lock logic verbatim rather than factoring it out — the two differ only in placement, and a shared version would be an abstraction over a two-line difference. Its corners don't all round the same way, per Overlay.dc.html's own callout: "a sheet keeps square corners against its edge" — only the two corners on the side facing the page take `--radius-lg` (`rounded-l-lg` for a right-hand sheet, `rounded-r-lg` for a left one), the two against the viewport edge stay square, and that same page-facing edge is the one that takes a `--color-gray-2` border Modal never draws.

<Popover/>

Free-form content floating beside the control that opened it.

kit/Floating.jsx

The middle term between a Tooltip and a Modal, and it earns its place by being the only one of the three that can hold CONTROLS. A Tooltip is a label and must never contain anything clickable — it disappears when the pointer leaves, so a button inside it is unreachable. A Modal blocks the page. A Popover does neither: it stays until dismissed, holds fields and buttons, and leaves the page live behind it.

align enum "start" start · center · end against the trigger. Default "center".
sideOffset number 8 gap from the trigger, in px — 8 for a popover, 6 for a tooltip: a popover is a panel, so it stands further off

open — a titled panel with a field and an action inside it

It takes `rounded-lg`, NOT `overlay-shape`, and that is a deliberate split from Modal. `overlay-shape` bundles a radius with a Modal-sized padding; a popover is compact, so it sets its own `p-4` and borrows only the radius rung. Everything else — `border-decor border-gray-2 shadow-overlay bg-surface text-secondary` — is shared exactly with DropdownMenu, because they are the same object (content floating over the page near where you asked for it) doing two jobs, not two different surfaces. Only their padding (`p-4` vs `p-1`) tells them apart. Nothing here reads the dead shadcn tokens (`bg-popover`, `text-popover-foreground`, `border-edge`) — everything reads Foundations' live `--color-*` tokens the way Card/Callout/Accordion do.

<Tooltip/>

A short label on hover — never anything you need to click.

kit/Floating.jsx

The one floating surface that does NOT share the popover treatment, and the exception is the point. Popover and DropdownMenu read `bg-surface`; a Tooltip reads `bg-secondary` with `text-white` — the exact pair Buttons.jsx's `strong` rank fills with, so a tooltip reads as the same kind of high-contrast ink as the rest of the language's emphasis vocabulary, not a fourth surface. It is not a panel you are working in, it is a label pinned to the thing under the cursor.

sideOffset number 6 tighter than Popover's — a tooltip belongs to the thing it labels

Rules that are not style preferences: it holds NO interactive content (it dismisses on pointer-leave, so a link inside is unreachable), and it never carries information available nowhere else — a tooltip is invisible to touch, to keyboard-only scanning and to anyone reading quickly. Use it to name an icon button, expand an abbreviation, or give a figure its units. `rounded-md` and a tight `px-2.5 py-1.5` keep it reading as a chip rather than a small card — and it carries NO shadow, on purpose. The mapping table is exhaustive per surface: the panel row names fill · edge · radius · shadow; the tooltip row names fill · ink · radius · text · padding and stops there — "the one floating thing that is not a panel." Don't re-add `shadow-overlay` here.

<Accordion/>

Sections that open one at a time — progressive disclosure, not a nav.

kit/Accordion.jsx

For content a reader can legitimately SKIP: an FAQ, advanced options, the older half of a history. It is the wrong tool for anything a reader must COMPARE, because comparison needs two panels open at once and single-mode closes one to open the next. It is also not navigation — collapsing your primary sections hides the shape of the page from whoever has not clicked yet. `variant` picks the anatomy: "list" (default) is a single shared white panel with hairline row dividers; "card" makes EACH item its own raised panel with a divider only above the open content; "filled" makes each item a flat gray tile with a 7px primary dot ahead of the question.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
type enum "multiple" "single" | "multiple" — single closes the open row when another opens; multiple lets them stack. Independent of variant.
defaultValue string "balance" which item starts open. Opening one by default is usually right — an all-closed accordion looks like an empty page.
collapsible boolean true whether the open row can be closed, leaving none open
variant enum "card" "list" | "card" | "filled" — on Accordion, inherited by every Item. Default "list".
items[].heading string "How is my balance calculated?" the question or section name, on AccordionTrigger — phrased so the closed state is still informative
items[].meta string "750 MB" on AccordionTrigger — a trailing muted value before the chevron
items[].body string "Accrual runs monthly…" the disclosed content, on AccordionContent

The open/close animation is a `grid-template-rows: 0fr → 1fr` transition rather than a max-height guess, and that is the one implementation detail worth copying: max-height forces you to name a number larger than the content, so every panel animates at a different real speed and a long one snaps at the end. The grid version measures itself. No part names a hex — every colour comes from Foundations, this component only decides which token belongs where. `meta` — a trailing muted value before the chevron — lives on `AccordionTrigger`, not on `Accordion`: it's "list" plus one per-row prop, not a fourth variant.

<AccordionItem · States/>

Two states past open/closed on a single row — inert, and needing attention.

kit/Accordion.jsx

`disabled` and `invalid` are per-Item, not per-Accordion — a caller marks one row, not the whole set. Neither is a variant: they compose with `list`/`card`/`filled` the same way any other row does. `invalid` does NOT force the item open — that stays a caller decision via `value`/`defaultValue`, same as any other row; the specimen below opens it only because its own `defaultValue` says so, not because invalid rows auto-expand.

disabled boolean true on AccordionItem. Trigger is inert (real disabled attribute) and drops to --color-border, no hover
invalid boolean true on AccordionItem. Danger label, chevron and content ink, plus a small stroke error glyph before the label. Hover still applies — only disabled suppresses it

Disabled sets the real HTML `disabled` attribute (not just a visual dim) and drops ink/chevron to `--color-border` with hover suppressed entirely — `bgInteractive` becomes bare `cursor-not-allowed`, not the usual `hover:bg-gray-1 active:bg-gray-2` pair every other row keeps. Invalid recolours ink, chevron AND the disclosed content to `--color-danger`, adds `aria-invalid="true"`, and prepends a small 14px stroke glyph (its own hand-drawn `<svg>`, no icon dependency — the same convention the chevron and Command's search glyph already use) ahead of the label. Unlike disabled, invalid keeps its hover wash — a plain affordance, not a diminished one.

<Separator/>

One hairline rule, horizontal or vertical.

kit/Layout.jsx

The least token-hungry component in the kit, and worth a page for exactly that reason: a rule should consume a border colour and nothing else. No language declares a separator, so there is no shape, no shadow and no radius to get wrong — only the question of WHICH border token it reads, and that one has a wrong answer.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
orientation enum "horizontal" horizontal · vertical — vertical needs a parent with a real height: it reads h-full, so in an auto-height row it collapses to nothing

horizontal — between two blocks of content

Vacation · 14 days remaining

Sick leave · 6 days remaining

  <p class="m-0 text-sm text-secondary">Vacation · 14 days remaining</p>
  <div role="separator" aria-orientation="horizontal" class="w-full h-px border-t border-gray-3 flex-none my-4"></div>
  <p class="m-0 text-sm text-text-muted">Sick leave · 6 days remaining</p>
</div>

vertical — between inline items, in a row with a height

Submitted
In review
Decided
markup 
<div class="flex h-6 items-center gap-4">
  <span class="text-sm text-secondary">Submitted</span>
  <div role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" class="h-full w-px border-l border-gray-3 flex-none"></div>
  <span class="text-sm text-secondary">In review</span>
  <div role="separator" aria-orientation="vertical" class="h-full w-px border-l border-gray-3 flex-none"></div>
  <span class="text-sm text-text-muted">Decided</span>
</div>

It reads `--color-gray-3`, NOT `--color-border` and NOT the card's own `border-decor`/`border-edge` pair. Layout.dc.html's own words: gray-3 is "the functional rule weight, one step stronger than a row divider" — the same step PageHeader's stat row and Table's header rule read. A separator is not an object's edge (that is the card contract, which cards themselves no longer even draw — see Cards.jsx), it is a rule INSIDE the page, and it needs the token that stays visibly a step stronger rather than the lighter one a container edge would use.

Identity #cat-identity

<StatusChip/>

A status tone as a pill, with an optional signal dot.

kit/Chips.jsx

FIVE tones, not seven — REDESIGNED 2026-08-13 off Chips.dc.html. tokens.css's Foundations rewrite names no `--tone-*` custom property any more, so there is nothing left for a token-based chip to resolve; every tone below is a literal Tailwind stock-palette class transcribed straight off Chips.jsx's own `TONES` object instead — `bg-emerald-50` / `text-emerald-700` / `bg-emerald-500` for success, and the same fill/ink/dot triplet in amber (warning), blue (info), rose (danger) and slate (neutral). Chips.jsx's own words: "Tones use Tailwind's own palette rather than a token of ours... and no Foundations entry to keep in sync." `pending` and `strong` are DROPPED, not renamed — "orange and near-black are actions here, not statuses" — an unrecognised tone now falls back to neutral rather than rendering unstyled.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
claim.status enum "approved" success · warning · info · danger · neutral — picks the tone. Closed set; anything else falls back to neutral.
claim.statusLabel string "Approved" the chip's text, not the raw enum value

neutral is the one exception to the -50/-700/-500 pattern the other four tones share: it reads slate-100/text-slate-700/bg-slate-400, one step darker across all three roles, because slate-50 is close enough to white to all but disappear on the card surface. Geometry is hardcoded literal Tailwind too, not the old `chip-shape`/`chip-dot` token bundle — `h-7 gap-1.5 px-3 text-sm` for the pill and a `size-1.75` dot at the (default) md size; `sm` drops to `h-6 gap-1.5 px-2.5 text-xs` and a `size-1.5` dot, off Tailwind's own spacing scale rather than a hand-picked pixel value. Dot and icon are mutually exclusive — icon wins if both are passed — and this renders a <span>, never a <button>: no hover state, no focus ring, nothing to click. A caller that needs a clickable status wants Button or Tab, not this.

<Avatar · AvatarStack/>

A person's initials in a tinted tile, always a circle.

kit/Avatar.jsx

REDESIGNED 2026-08-13 from Avatar.dc.html — settles the three-way disagreement the old entry here used to document (Beacon circle vs. Checkpoint rounded-square vs. Nimbus absent): this app renders Beacon alone now, so there is one shape, a circle, `--radius-avatar` (9999px, full). `size` is NEW — xs|sm|md|lg — and reads Tailwind's OWN `size-6/8/10/14` scale directly rather than a custom `--avatar-size` token: 6/8/10/14 × the 4px `--spacing` base is 24/32/40/56px, and initials land on Tailwind's stock `text-2xs/xs/sm/lg` (10/12/14/18px) for the same reason, no token needed. `md` (40px) is the default, unchanged from before.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
assignee.name string "R. Iyer" derives initials — "R. Iyer" → RI, single word "Mary" → MA. No name renders an em dash, never an empty tile.
assignee.initials string "KF" override the derivation, e.g. for a team rather than a person
assignee.tone enum "danger" success · warning · info · danger — the same map Card and StatusChip read. No tone (or "neutral") is an explicit neutral tile, not an absence. `pending`/`strong` are gone.
size enum "lg" xs · sm · md · lg — 24/32/40/56px tiles, initials scale with the tile and stay bold. "md" is the default.

No tone (or tone="neutral") is NOT "no fill" — it is an explicit neutral tile, `bg-gray-1` fill / `text-secondary` ink, the honest default for a person with nothing attached; an empty/transparent circle was never on the table. Four tinted tones beyond that (success/warning/info/danger) read the SAME map Card and StatusChip do — `var(--color-<tone>-bg)` / `var(--color-<tone>-ink)` — so an owner's tile can carry its row's status colour exactly. `pending` and `strong` are GONE, not renamed: Foundations' tone map never named either, so both now fall through to neutral. A missing name falls back to an em dash, never an empty circle — "an empty tile reads as a loading state that never resolves." AvatarStack renders every tile fixed at `sm` (32px) with a quarter-tile overlap (-9px, scaled from the doc's own -11px/40px ratio) and a 2px ring read through Tailwind's own `ring-surface` utility, so a stack under a caller that overrides `--color-surface` still looks right with no extra prop; `max` renders a "+N" overflow tile in `bg-gray-1` / `text-text-muted` / `font-mono`.

<Breadcrumb/>

An ancestor trail. Draws no navigation of any kind.

kit/Breadcrumb.jsx

[SOURCE] Breadcrumb.dc.html — REDESIGNED 2026-08-13. The old entry here explained that none of the three retired languages named a breadcrumb at all, so every decision was [OURS]; that is no longer true, Breadcrumb.dc.html is its own page now with an explicit token-mapping table: an ancestor link is `--color-text-muted` / `text-xs` / no underline, hovering to `--color-secondary`; the current page is `--color-secondary` / `font-semibold` / `aria-current="page"` and never a link; the chevron-right separator and the NEW ellipsis both read `--color-border` — "the same weight as the separator, since it is one"; the trail gap is `gap-1.5`; a link's focus ring is `--color-ring` / `ring-2` / `--radius-sm` — "since the target is text."

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
claim.category string "Marine" an ancestor crumb, linked
claim.id string "CLM-4417" the current page's leaf crumb — inert, aria-current="page"
maxItems number 4 Past this many items, collapses the middle to a single "…" and keeps the first item plus the last two.
homeIcon boolean true Draws a Lucide house icon beside the first item's label.

`maxItems` and `homeIcon` are both NEW. `maxItems` collapses the MIDDLE, not a truncation from one end — first item + ellipsis + last two, "those are the ones people actually click" — and only fires once there's an actual middle to hide (more than 3 items); with `maxItems={4}` and exactly 4 items there's nothing to collapse, so all four still render. `homeIcon` draws a real Lucide house icon beside the FIRST item's label specifically, which after a collapse is still index 0. The separator is a real Lucide `chevron-right` icon now, not a hand-drawn SVG wedge — "a text character shifts its weight and baseline with the font, where an icon sits identically at any size." The leaf is still deliberately inert regardless of href — the style guide's own page identity is a plain heading, so an unclickable current-page item matches it, and it is the accessible behaviour regardless.

Process #cat-process

<Stepper · Timeline · ActivityFeed/>

The three ways a process shows its shape.

kit/Feed.jsx

ONE entry rather than three, because they answer the same question at three scales and only make sense compared. They are separate COMPONENTS for a reason that is easy to lose: a Stepper is a CLOSED sequence with a current position — the steps are known in advance and identical for every record, so it runs horizontally and the eye reads progress left to right. A Timeline is an OPEN history — nobody knows how many events there will be, so it runs vertically down a rail that simply keeps going. Fusing them, which the old cookbook recipe did, forces the open case to pretend it has an end and the closed case to hide the one thing it knows. ActivityFeed is the Timeline with an actor: same rail mechanic, a 30px avatar instead of an icon marker, because "who" is the column the eye scans first. REDESIGNED 2026-08-13 off Feed.dc.html: every marker grew from a 7px chip-dot riding a bare `border-l` to a 30px tone-tinted circle sitting on its own rail column, and Stepper picked up `onStep` — a step renders as a real `<button>` iff a caller passes one, exactly Card's own opt-in `clickable` rule, and is otherwise exactly as inert as it always was.

fieldtypeexamplewhat it drives
steps array<{label,meta?}> | string[] { label: "In repair", meta: "in progress" } Stepper: the closed sequence, in order. A bare string is accepted as a label with no meta.
current number 2 Stepper: index of the step in progress. Done steps read --color-primary fill with a check (never the ticked-off number); ahead steps read --color-gray-1, muted, in mono; only the current step takes the +2px inset ring.
onStep (index, step) => void (i, step) => setCurrent(i) NEW. Supplying it renders every step as a real <button> — click-to-jump. Omit it and a step is exactly as inert as it always was, same as Card's own opt-in clickable rule.
items array<{title,meta,body?,tone?,icon?}> { title: "Claim rejected by assessor", meta: "16 Jul · 14:22", tone: "danger" } Timeline: newest first. The 30px marker reads var(--color-<tone>-bg/-ink) — success · warning · info · danger only; neutral/unset/unrecognised falls back to gray-1/text-muted. Empty renders "No events.", never a blank list.
items[].icon ReactNode <AlertTriangleIcon /> Timeline only. Omit it and the marker falls back to a small currentColor dot — dot vs icon, never both, the same rule Callout uses.
items[].body string "Seal replacement not covered under the extended warranty terms." Timeline only, optional — renders only when present.
activity array<{actor,action,object?,tone?,meta,body?,attachment?}> { actor: "R. Iyer", action: "rejected", object: "CLM-4417", meta: "16 Jul · 14:22", tone: "danger" } ActivityFeed: bold actor, then the sentence. The marker takes actor.slice(0,2), uppercased — "R. Iyer" reads "R.", punctuation included. Feed.jsx's own initials rule, not Avatar's first+last-letter one.
activity[].object string "CLM-4417" An id/reference, set in mono — "data, not prose." Additive: omit it and the sentence is exactly the plain action it always was.
activity[].body string "Docking invoice attached — needs sign-off before Friday." The person's own words, in a plain --color-gray-1 block — no tail, no border. Renders only when present; a bare action gets no block at all.
activity[].attachment {name,size?} { name: "drydock-invoice.pdf", size: "1.2 MB" } A file row under the note, on its OWN surface (--color-surface + --shadow-contact) so it doesn't fuse into the identical gray note block above it.
onAttachment (attachment, item) => void (file, item) => download(file) Supplying it adds the download control beside the file row. Omit it and the row is a label, not a promise the prototype can't keep.

Stepper, current={2} — a CLOSED sequence: horizontal above sm, stacked below, and only the current step takes the ring.
